_experiment.description: Width scaling — hidden layers widened from 10 to 50 neurons. Total prunable weights: 196*50 + 50*50 + 50*10 = 12300, vs 2160 in the baseline. The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis predicts that wider overparameterised networks contain more redundant sub-networks, so the flat (compensation-complete) region of the sparsity curve should extend much further before accuracy degrades. The per-layer NZ columns in the log reveal which layer the algorithm preferentially prunes.
literature: Wang et al. 2020 (Lottery Ticket): winning tickets exist in overparameterised networks — wider networks should have more tickets and thus tolerate more pruning
Blalock et al. 2020 (survey): compression ratios in the literature are frequently not accompanied by measured latency improvements — this experiment establishes what sparsity ratio is achievable
